hints: Notice the question labels $6.0\text{ V}$ as e.m.f. in the cell and $6.0\text{ V}$ as p.d. across the resistor, so track where charge gains and loses energy.
Recall that $1\text{ V} = 1\text{ J C}^{-1}$, so both e.m.f. and p.d. must be described as energy transferred per unit charge, not total energy.
Link the direction of transfer to the component: chemical to electrical in the cell for e.m.f., electrical to thermal in the resistor for p.d.
walkthrough: Identify the setup: a $6.0\text{ V}$ cell of negligible internal resistance connected only to a resistor, so charge gains energy in the cell and loses the same amount per coulomb in the resistor.
State the definitions: e.m.f. $E = W/Q$ is work done on charge per unit charge by the source, and p.d. $V = W/Q$ is work done by charge per unit charge in the load.
Check units: $\text{V}$ means $\text{J C}^{-1}$, so any statement calling e.m.f. or p.d. simply the energy transferred is incomplete.
Assign the correct energy conversion: in the cell chemical energy becomes electrical potential energy of charge, in the resistor electrical energy becomes thermal energy.
Combine both points: only the statement with per unit charge and chemical to electrical for e.m.f. plus electrical to thermal for p.d. is fully correct. This is option C.

options.A: Correct energy changes are identified but $6.0\text{ V}$ is not total energy, it is energy per unit charge in $\text{J C}^{-1}$.
options.B: The processes are swapped and the per unit charge part is missing: p.d. does not create electrical energy in the cell.
options.C: E.m.f. is work done on charge in the cell and p.d. is work done by charge in the resistor, both measured as energy per unit charge.
options.D: Includes per unit charge but swaps the locations: e.m.f. belongs to the cell and p.d. belongs to the resistor.
